 News › News News › CBSE Date Sheet 2027 Out in This Month! Latest updates on CBSE 10th, 12th board exams CBSE Date Sheet 2027 Out in This Month! Latest updates on CBSE 10th, 12th board exams
 Jasleen Taneja Updated: Nov 2, 2026, 11:40 IST CBSE Date Sheet 2026 to be released in December 2026 CBSE Date Sheet 2027 Latest Updates - The Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) will release the CBSE date sheet 2027 on the official website- cbse.nic.in. The CBSE exam dates 2027 for Classes 10, 12 will be announced in December 2026 . the exams will commence from February 15, 2027 and will be conducted in pen and paper format.
 According to a Board official , CBSE has just completed the LOC that shares the list of candidates along with their subjects they will appear for. The Board will now prepare the CBSE date sheet 2027 and is expected to release it by late December 2026 or early January 2027 . "The exams will likely be held between February 15 and April first week 2027 . Students must check the official website regularly for all latest updates on the release of CBSE date sheet," she told.
 Students preparing for the CBSE Board exams 2027 class 10, 12 must finish with all the topics mentioned in the CBSE syllabus 2027. They must also download and go through the important questions released by the Board that can be asked in the exams. For better preparations, students must solve and practice the CBSE sample papers 2027 and previous years question papers (PYQPs). Many CBSE schools have released the date sheet for the pre-board 1 exams to be held in their schools.

 CBSE Class 10 Exam pattern 2028 Revised
 The Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) has revised the CBSE 10th exam pattern for students who will take the Class 10 board exams in 2028. The board has clarified that three subjects will not form part of the curriculum for this batch: Individuals in Society , the Modules on Computational Thinking (CT) and AI , and Environmental Education .
 Board officials said the subjects had created confusion among students and added to the burden of studying nine to 10 subjects. With the clarification, students can concentrate on five subjects for the board exams and learn the others without the pressure of scoring marks.
